summary: Catahoula Parish, LA tower built 1929; a 1929 report says International Paper land, a 1941 survey says Southern Kraft; Wikipedia says possibly torn down.

facts.design: 90-foot steel tower of standard lookout tower construction
facts.status_note: Wikipedia lists it as possibly torn down (question mark) and says aerial imagery could not confirm it

events.note: 1929 newspaper report says it was being erected in October 1929; the 1941 survey description says it was built in 1929
Rainfall totals reported as recorded at the tower in 1955 and 1957 newspaper items
Removed from USGS maps according to Wikipedia; the list gives no date for the tower coming down

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1929 report places the tower on International Paper Company lands; the 1941 survey description says it was owned by Southern Kraft Corporation. The record keeps both names and does not resolve how they relate.

sources.title: List of fire lookout towers in Louisiana

notes_for_editor: Build year is supported by two sources (1929 newspaper, 1941 NGS description). Staffing is only a 1929 plan; no later source says who manned it. Rain totals are from 1955 and 1957 newspaper items as quoted on the Central US Lookouts page; not checked against the original papers. Fate is uncertain: Wikipedia marks it torn down with a question mark. The Wikipedia location (northeast of Jena) and the 1929 report (near the La Salle Parish line) are not reconciled. No current site description found. The firetower.org Louisiana register lists six registered sites and none of them is Aimwell.
